A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSO research. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original preference-tuning experiments in Tables 1–3 and generated examples for style transfer and concept customization, including appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds preference-baseline scores and quantitative concept-customization results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The task-specific training procedures are substantively revised. Concept customization changes from Eq. 3 with reverse-sampled reference trajectories to offline PSO with pretrained reference-model terms removed and prior-preservation loss added (Sections 3.3/B.3). Style transfer changes from offline PSO to Eq. 3 with reverse trajectories sampled each step (Sections 3.2/B.2), although residual offline wording creates ambiguity. The general PSO equations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pick-a-Pic v2 and PartiPrompts for preference tuning/evaluation, Pokemon for style transfer, and Dreambooth examples for customization. Quantifying customization in v3 does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated SDXL-SFT, SDXL-RPO, SDXL-SPO and SDXL-MaPO comparators on both preference benchmarks. New Table 4 compares PSO customization against Dreambooth with SDXL and SDXL-Turbo, substantially expanding the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: V3 adds quantitative customization evaluation using CLIP-T, DINO and CLIP-I, replacing exclusively qualitative assessment of that task. Appendix B.1 changes the reported online training budget from 15k to 20k steps. Table 1 newly specifies 50-step multi-step baselines, conflicting with the retained 25-step prose. These are reported protocol changes; the unchanged earlier scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 newly reports an unquantified observation that removing the reference model and adding prior-preservation loss improves customization. This provides a limited component-comparison claim without an isolated ablation table. Existing one-versus-four-step generalization checks and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the fixed generation-seed statement and average-score reporting. Neither introduces repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands reported results through the additional Table 1 baseline rows and first quantitative customization comparison. Table 4 reports CLIP-T/DINO/CLIP-I of 0.271/0.593/0.733 for four-step PSO, alongside two Dreambooth baselines. Previously reported scores in Tables 1–3 and the generated images remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, the PSO derivation and the SDXL-Turbo MDP formulation are retained. Clarifying the pretrained-model notation and adding pseudocode do not introduce new mathematical assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the principal claims: directly tuning timestep-distilled models, unifying offline and online preference optimization, and supporting preference tuning, style transfer and customization.

C2.justification: V2 already suggests improving personalization and exploring controllable generation. V3 additionally states a specific limitation: style transfer and customization require further loss-design and regularization work to achieve more competitive image quality.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository link and Algorithms 1–3 documenting the existing PSO variants. Appendix B.3 additionally specifies using images from the initial model for prior preservation. These improve access instructions and procedural documentation; repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 expands discussion and citations covering foundational distillation, self-play diffusion tuning, customization and parameter-efficient adaptation, and adds RPO/MaPO references. These extend the existing positioning; the central distinction from tuning multi-step diffusion models remains.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and cross-reference corrections, adds pseudocode references and a limitations paragraph, expands related-work passages, and shortens the ethical statement. The overall section structure and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 4 and three algorithm displays, expands Table 1, adds inference-step columns to Tables 1–2, and restores the missing Pickapic Test label in Table 3. Existing figures are retained with relocation, layout adjustments and a corrected Figure 3 model label.

improvement.justification: The expanded baselines and first quantitative customization comparison strengthen empirical assessment, while pseudocode, a code pointer and specific limitations improve documentation. The gains are constrained by conflicting 25-versus-50-step descriptions and inconsistent offline-versus-reverse-trajectory wording for style transfer. V3 therefore offers a limited net improvement rather than a fully resolved evaluation and reproducibility account.
